title: The law of the Church joins mission, morals, and consecration
setting: Joseph Smith had reached Kirtland, Ohio, only days earlier, and many new converts were waiting for direction. Earlier revelations had promised that the law would be given once the Saints gathered in Ohio. On 9 February 1831 twelve elders met, prayed together, and asked practical questions about gathering, governance, and property. Joseph dictated verses 1–72 in their presence. The Joseph Smith Papers date verses 74–93 to 23 February, when Joseph and seven elders asked how to apply the law.
summary: The revelation calls itself a law and first sends every elder except Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to preach two by two. Edward Partridge keeps his office, and no one may preach unless ordained by someone with known authority. Teachers are to teach from the Bible and the Book of Mormon, and only by the Spirit. Then it gives moral laws against killing, stealing, lying, lust, adultery, and speaking evil. It commands the Saints to consecrate property to the bishop for the poor, each becoming a steward of what he receives. Surplus goes to a storehouse for the needy, for lands, and for building the New Jerusalem. It adds rules on plain dress, idleness, care for the sick, and seeking revelation. The later verses set procedures for church discipline and for handing crimes to the law of the land.

contextNote.title: Consecration as a way to remember the poor
contextNote.text: The elders had asked how to provide for families and for members coming from New York. Verse 30 answers with a command to “remember the poor” and consecrate property for their support. It binds the gift “with a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken”. Verse 32 then returns to each giver a stewardship sufficient for his family. Verse 38 gives the reason behind the system: what is done for “the least of these” is done for Christ. In this passage, consecration is a legal transfer of property joined to a religious covenant.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 41–44 uses verses 30–42 to show how early Saints cared for those in need. Verse 38 says serving “the least of these” is serving Christ; how could verses 40–42 shape your own use of time and money?
reviewNote: Read all 93 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, two parts on 9 and 23 February 1831, the first in the presence of twelve elders, fulfilling D&C 38:32. JSP introduction to the 9 February text supplied the elders’ questions and notes the second part is a separate JSP document, “Revelation, 23 February 1831 [D&C 42:74–93]” (found via search, not loaded). JSP does not explain verse 73’s origin, so the setting avoids dating it.
